sentences.text: Tristychius was a small animal reaching a maximum length of about 60 cm.
This creature possessed a heterocercal tail fin, a structure where the upper lobe is larger than the lower, and large spines on its two dorsal fins.
Fossils of the only known species, Tristychius arcuatus, including fin spines, have been discovered in Scotland.
The genus Tristychius was described by Agassiz in 1837.
Topic: diet. Scientists estimate it was a specialized suction-feeding benthic predator that likely captured food by creating a vacuum to draw prey into its mouth.
Tristychius belongs to the class Chondrichthyes, the group containing modern sharks and rays.
Although historically classified as a hybodont, a 2016 study reclassified Tristychius as a basal euselachian, noting that hybodonts are more closely related to modern sharks and rays.
It is placed in the family Tristychiidae alongside the genus Acronemus.
Tristychius lived during the Visean to Serpukhovian stages, between 346.7 and 326.9 million years ago.
